objectives.en: Find the speed of a transverse wave on a string
Find the speed of sound; explain Laplace's correction

narration.en: A veena player turns the peg to tighten a string and the note goes up. Tension changes how fast waves run along the string.
narration.kn: ವೀಣಾ ವಾದಕ ಗೂಟ ತಿರುಗಿಸಿ ತಂತಿ ಬಿಗಿಗೊಳಿಸಿದಾಗ ಸ್ವರ ಏರುತ್ತದೆ. ತಂತಿಯ ಮೇಲೆ ತರಂಗಗಳು ಎಷ್ಟು ವೇಗವಾಗಿ ಸಾಗುತ್ತವೆ ಎಂಬುದನ್ನು ಎಳೆತ ಬದಲಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.

body.en: The speed of a transverse wave on a stretched string depends only on the tension T and the mass per unit length μ: v = √(T/μ). Tension provides the restoring force and μ the inertia. It does not depend on the frequency; the source decides the frequency, and the wavelength then adjusts as λ = v/ν.
body.kn: ಎಳೆದ ತಂತಿಯ ಮೇಲಿನ ಅಡ್ಡ ತರಂಗದ ಜವ v = √(T/μ). ಎಳೆತ ಪುನಃಸ್ಥಾಪಕ ಬಲ ನೀಡುತ್ತದೆ, μ ಜಡತ್ವ ನೀಡುತ್ತದೆ. ಜವ ಆವೃತ್ತಿಯನ್ನು ಅವಲಂಬಿಸುವುದಿಲ್ಲ.

title.en: A travelling wave on a string

narration.en: The shape moves along the string, but each bit of string only goes up and down. Watch the red bead. Change the frequency or the speed and see how the wavelength changes, because speed equals frequency times wavelength.
narration.kn: ಆಕಾರ ದಾರದ ಉದ್ದಕ್ಕೂ ಚಲಿಸುತ್ತದೆ, ಆದರೆ ದಾರದ ಪ್ರತಿ ಭಾಗ ಮೇಲೆ ಕೆಳಗೆ ಮಾತ್ರ ಹೋಗುತ್ತದೆ. ಕೆಂಪು ಮಣಿ ನೋಡಿ. ವೇಗ = ಆವೃತ್ತಿ × ತರಂಗದೂರ.

caption.en: The string follows y = A sin(kx − ωt), with k = 2π/λ and ω = 2πf. The shape moves at v = fλ; the red bead only moves up and down.
caption.kn: ದಾರ y = A sin(kx − ωt) ಅನುಸರಿಸುತ್ತದೆ, k = 2π/λ, ω = 2πf. ಆಕಾರ v = fλ ವೇಗದಲ್ಲಿ ಚಲಿಸುತ್ತದೆ; ಕೆಂಪು ಮಣಿ ಮೇಲೆ ಕೆಳಗೆ ಮಾತ್ರ.

tryThis.en: Double the frequency. What happens to the wavelength?
Pause, then scrub time slowly: does the red bead ever move sideways?
tryThis.kn: ವಿರಾಮ ಮಾಡಿ, ಸಮಯವನ್ನು ನಿಧಾನವಾಗಿ ಸರಿಸಿ: ಕೆಂಪು ಮಣಿ ಪಕ್ಕಕ್ಕೆ ಸರಿಯುತ್ತದೆಯೇ?

tryThis.en: Follow one crest and time it over 4 m. Is it the speed you set?
tryThis.kn: ಒಂದು ಶೃಂಗ ಹಿಂಬಾಲಿಸಿ 4 m ಗೆ ಸಮಯ ಅಳೆಯಿರಿ. ನೀವು ಹೊಂದಿಸಿದ ವೇಗವೇ?

title.en: What sets the speed of a wave

say.en: A string with mass per unit length mu is stretched over a pulley by a hanging load. The tension T pulls it back; mu resists.
Only T and mu matter, and dimensions fix the answer: T over mu has units of a speed squared.
A steel wire 0.72 metre long of mass 5 grams under a tension of 60 newton: the speed is about 93 metres per second.
Sound in a fluid travels at root of B over rho. Newton took B = P, as if the compressions were isothermal, and got only about 280 metres per second.
Laplace: the compressions are too fast for heat to flow, so they are adiabatic and B = gamma P. That gives about 332 metres per second, matching experiment.

narration.en: A string with mass per unit length mu is stretched over a pulley by a hanging load. The tension T pulls it back; mu resists. Only T and mu matter, and dimensions fix the answer: T over mu has units of a speed squared. A steel wire 0.72 metre long of mass 5 grams under a tension of 60 newton: the speed is about 93 metres per second. Sound in a fluid travels at root of B over rho. Newton took B = P, as if the compressions were isothermal, and got only about 280 metres per second. Laplace: the compressions are too fast for heat to flow, so they are adiabatic and B = gamma P. That gives about 332 metres per second, matching experiment.

body.en: Longitudinal waves travel at v = √(B/ρ) in a fluid and √(Y/ρ) in a solid rod. Newton assumed the compressions in air were isothermal (B = P) and got about 280 m s⁻¹, too low. Laplace pointed out they are so fast that they are adiabatic (B = γP), giving v = √(γP/ρ) ≈ 331 m s⁻¹ at 0 °C, which matches experiment. For a gas, v does not depend on pressure at a fixed temperature, and v ∝ √T.
body.kn: ನೀಳ ತರಂಗದ ಜವ ದ್ರವದಲ್ಲಿ √(B/ρ), ಘನ ಸರಳಿನಲ್ಲಿ √(Y/ρ). ನ್ಯೂಟನ್ ಸಮೋಷ್ಣೀಯ ಎಂದು ಭಾವಿಸಿ 280 m s⁻¹ ಪಡೆದರು. ಲ್ಯಾಪ್ಲಾಸ್ ಅಡಿಯಾಬ್ಯಾಟಿಕ್ ಎಂದು ತಿದ್ದಿ v = √(γP/ρ) ≈ 331 m s⁻¹ ಪಡೆದರು. v ∝ √T.

points.en: v ∝ √T; independent of P at fixed T

body.en: v ∝ √T (kelvin). Near room temperature the speed of sound in air rises by about 0.6 m s⁻¹ for each degree Celsius.

narration.en: Temperature shortcut for sound. v ∝ √T (kelvin). Near room temperature the speed of sound in air rises by about 0.6 m s⁻¹ for each degree Celsius.
A stretched string must carry waves at exactly 100 m/s. Choose its tension and its mass per unit length.

prompt.en: A stretched string must carry waves at exactly 100 m/s. Choose its tension and its mass per unit length.

explanation.en: v = √(T/μ) = √(100/0.01) = 100 m/s. Doubling μ needs double the tension.
